subject: issues with function signature error dump

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: issues with function signature error dump
parts:
I built the basic version, but there are a few catches.

For the recent example on the users list, we get
what we want as output from this model:

-------------------------------------------------
model {
real x[5];
2 ~ categorical(softmax(x));
}

EXPECTATION FAILURE LOCATION: file=../temp2/dumb.stan; line=3, column=29

2 ~ categorical(softmax(x));
^-- here


DIAGNOSTIC(S) FROM PARSER:
no matches for function name="softmax"
arg 0 type=real[1]
available function signatures for softmax:
0. softmax(vector) : vector
expression is ill formed
Parser expecting: <eps>
------------------------------------------------------



Next, consider errors in sampling statements, as in:

model {
1 ~ normal();
}

When I just print everything out, I get all 64
signatures for normal_log. I don't see a way around
that.

But I think the change of notation with normal() becoming normal_log()
and the variate (here 1) becoming the first argument with an implicit
real return is going to be confusing. On the plus side, it matches
our LaTeX index :-)

Now consider this model, which contains another error we've
seen on the users list recently:

model {
real x;
vector[3] y;
x <- 1 / y;
}

The problem here is that the operator "/" is used, but
the function implicated is "divide". Here's the error output:

------------------------------------------------------------------

EXPECTATION FAILURE LOCATION: file=../temp2/dumb.stan; line=4, column=13

x <- 1 / y;
^-- here


DIAGNOSTIC(S) FROM PARSER:
no matches for function name="divide"
arg 0 type=int
arg 1 type=vector
available function signatures for divide:
0. divide(real, real) : real
1. divide(vector, real) : vector
2. divide(row vector, real) : row vector
3. divide(matrix, real) : matrix
expression is ill formed
Parser expecting: <eps>
------------------------------------------------------------------


There's also the issue that we may mislead them with the int vs.
real arguments, because Stan allows int values to be promoted to
real values as necessary.

This is going to be harder than I thought it would be to do well!

- Bob
